They believed in Jesus because of Himself - because of His character, and the light that came from Him, and also because of the light of their own inspiration within themselves.

order.why: Consider qualities as evidence of reality.
Distinguish the sun from its shadow.
Read character, deeds and words together.
Keep the reported exchange about truth.
Let ocean and sun convey independence.
Read verses as the way of recognition.
Preserve the seal’s declaration.
Connect seal, Self and Cause.
shortened: My blessed seal is My proof, My Self My evidence, My Cause My testimony, and My resplendent beauty.

order.why: Consider independence from earlier books.
Read independence beside the Hidden Book.
Keep attention on the fundamental proof.
shortened: In such circumstances, man must at all times fix his gaze upon the fundamental proof of God and that whereby all proofs have been established, lest he be veiled from the Source of Revelation and all his deeds and actions be rendered null and void while he remaineth unaware.

order.why: Examine the Book’s own standard.
Consider utterance’s testimony to its nature.
Read the extended Iqan arguments.
shortened: If thou wilt grasp the implication of this verse, thou wilt recognize the truth that no manifestation greater than the Prophets of God hath ever been revealed, and no testimony mightier than the testimony of their revealed verses hath ever appeared upon the earth.
The proof of the sun is the light thereof, which shineth and envelopeth all things. The evidence of the shower is the bounty thereof, which reneweth and investeth the world with the mantle of life.

And yet, is not the object of every Revelation to effect a transformation in the whole character of mankind, a transformation that shall manifest itself, both outwardly and inwardly, that shall affect both its inner life and external conditions? For if the character of mankind be not changed, the futility of God's universal Manifestation would be apparent.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s argument from verses.
shortened: And by the very same proof which aforetimes the prophethood of Muhammad, blessings of God rest upon Him, was vindicated, Their return to the world is also proven in the sight of God and those who are endued with knowledge. That supreme proof is naught but the revelation of the verses, which is beyond the power of all dwellers on earth to produce the like thereof.

Moreover, the proof of revealed verses doth, alone and of itself, conclusively demonstrate the utter impotence of all created things on earth, for this is a proof which hath proceeded from God and shall endure until the Day of Resurrection.

order.why: Compare demanded miracles with the Quranic criterion.
shortened: Yet they say: "The Proof of God was not made complete for us in the Bayan through signs." How then do ye, by that same Proof, seek to convince him who would enter your Faith? And ye have not beheld Muhammad, the Messenger of God, nor have ye witnessed in all your lives any proof other than that Proof. How, then, do ye believe therein and are assured?

order.why: Read the Seven Proofs on consistency.
shortened: Be fair - what difference is there between the time when thou first knew thyself and became adherent to thy religion through the proof of the Qur'an, and when thou looked upon the Bayan yet did not believe?
Even as thou didst behold a verse from the Bayan, by the same proof through which thou didst become faithful to the religion of the Qur'an, it is incumbent upon thee to believe in those verses.

Consider now the Revelation of the Bayan: had the people of the Qur'an applied to themselves the same arguments they use against those who differ from their faith, not a single soul would have remained veiled, and all would have attained salvation on the Day of Resurrection.

order.why: Consider the challenge to equal the Book.
shortened: Were humans and jinn to gather together to produce the like of this Book in truth, they would never be able, even if they had all the people of earth and their like besides as helpers. By thy True Lord! They shall never be able to produce the like of even a portion of its letters, nor of its interpretations from some of the mystery, even as much as the film of a date-stone.

order.why: Hear the parallel challenge concerning this Tablet.
Read the Arabic Seven Proofs.
Join truth-seeking with equitable discourse.
Examine the Quran’s own arguments.
shortened: And after Muhammad, the Messenger of God, was taken, there was no proof with you except the Furqan (Qur'an). Therefore, look within it - did God ever argue without a verse?

order.why: Keep the prayer about continuity of proof.
Consider common letters and incomparable verses.
shortened: Consider that the nineteen letters were in everyone's possession, yet none could speak verses like Mine. Indeed, I have made all My verses a proof for all who dwell on earth. Have you heard, from the first wondrous day of Adam - peace be upon him - until now, of anyone writing a single page that would serve as proof for all in the heavens and earth?

order.why: Read language, upbringing and revelation together.
shortened: By My life, the Cause of God in respect to Me is more wondrous than the Cause of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, before Me, would ye but reflect upon it. Say: He was raised among the Arabs, then after forty years God revealed verses unto Him and made Him His Messenger to all the worlds. Say: I was raised among the Persians, and God revealed unto Me, after twenty-five years of My life had passed, verses which all are powerless to produce.

order.why: Examine the unpremeditated utterance challenge.
shortened: Consider within yourself: if you can speak everything you wish without reflection, and write whatever you desire without pause of the pen, and transform a single verse into well-constructed words reaching seventy in number, then you speak the truth in your claim. Otherwise, seek forgiveness from your Lord and return to His judgment.

order.why: Keep the reported immediate invitation to ask.
Read the reported argument to Muslim hearers.
shortened: The seven proofs laid down by the Blessed Perfection of His truth are especially addressed to Mussulmen. The Koran is indisputable proof of Mahomet. If one is in doubt of this, he has only to produce a chapter of it. If this is so, then do not the writing of the Blessed Perfection prove His truth?

order.why: Consider the reported abundance of revelation.
Read the Bab’s response through its signs.
shortened: If thou makest proof to be the mention of visions, as thou hast done in thy book, then by the glory of thy Lord, I have written more than thou in well-known books.

And if thou makest proof to be eloquence in the mentioned sermon, then by thy Lord, I have composed sermons that none hath mentioned before and none today can match, as until now there have flowed from my pen some thirty pages of prayers, sermons, holy allusions, glorified signs, paradisiacal stations, and prescribed verses.

order.why: Keep the Tabriz examination account attributed.
Read recitation and opposition in the Seven Proofs.
shortened: From the Pen of Holiness hath flowed the declaration that, in this Day, these verses -- sent down from the clouds of majesty -- are the conclusive proof unto the East and unto the West of the world, and that no testimony above them hath ever been, nor ever shall be, vouchsafed. Even as the Crown Prince summoned that Essence of Eternality to his court and demanded proof, that Ancient Beauty declared that the verses were the testimony. Yet in the end they accepted it not, and all pronounced sentence of death upon that Quintessence of pre-existence, save a few who became assured through the divine verses and turned from the west of unbelief and error to the east of faith and recognition.

order.why: Attend to witnessing a newly revealed text.
shortened: In service to the opposers, this servant offers two words: Let some be appointed as representatives by others and come to this land, but on condition that they possess their own eyes and ears, as they are commanded in this Revelation, and witness that which equals all previous books and accept it. And if they desire, another equivalent can be newly revealed, provided all acknowledge that these verses did not exist before and have descended from the heaven of divine nature.

order.why: Connect lack of schooling with claimed knowledge.
shortened: Say: We have not entered schools, yet We have sent down from the heaven of knowledge and wisdom that before which all the learning of the earth hath bowed down, as every discerning one doth testify.

order.why: Read the account of varied scholarly questions.
shortened: O thou who gazest upon the Kingdom of God! In the days when the Ancient Beauty and the Most Great Name illumined the horizon of Iraq with the lights of His dawning, all the leaders of the peoples - whether scholars, men of learning, princes or nobles - would present themselves in His holy court and verbally pose their most difficult and complex questions. These would be answered immediately from His pure lips with the most wondrous utterance and perfect exposition.

For instance, a Jewish scholar would ask a most difficult question from the Torah and would immediately receive an answer. A Christian scholar would pose a complex question from the Gospel and would be convinced by His very utterance. A learned exponent of the Qur'an would present himself and earnestly seek clarification of whatever most difficult questions he had in mind, and like parched earth receiving the descent of pure water, would attain satisfaction. Similarly would come the mystic, the philosopher, the mathematician, the physician, the engineer, the man of letters, and the poet - even scholars of geography.

order.why: Keep the reported mathematical claim attributed.
Consider knowledge and verses separately.
shortened: If they look to knowledge, its sun is manifest and evident from the horizons of divine Tablets in such wise that none hath any way to deny or object. And if they look to verses, these have encompassed East and West.

order.why: Locate the invitation within named periods.
shortened: Say: If ye desire verses, they have indeed filled the horizons, and if ye seek clear proofs, read ye what hath been sent down from My Pen when the Wronged One was in Zawra (Baghdad) and in this mighty, exalted Station.

order.why: Allow this Tablet’s own claim to stand.
Consider the appointment of future standards.
shortened: Until this Manifestation, verses alone have been proof for all, for We had sent down this decree in all previous Books.

Although in this Manifestation all signs of power, manifest proofs, wondrous verses, glorious manifestations and divine attributes have appeared - and all this as a grace from Us to all created things - yet henceforth the matter resteth in God's hands, that He may designate what shall be proof for future Manifestations.

order.why: Distinguish clear evidence from its appointed form.
shortened: He has established these Dawning-Places that have risen from the Morn of Oneness with such clear proof that none besides these holy Manifestations could produce the like thereof, leaving no room for rejection or objection. For divine proof and heavenly evidence would not be complete for human beings without clear proof and manifest evidence. However, the specific nature of that proof - whether revealed verses, apparent signs, or otherwise - has been and always will be dependent on the will of that King of Divine Will alone, and not contingent upon any other.

order.why: Apply proofs across successive Prophets.
Read the detailed challenge to inconsistency.
shortened: By the same proof by which they believe and are certain of the Primal Point, we believe and are certain of the very Manifestation with something even greater.

And if you do not look to the Bayan and deny God's proof which all the Prophets and Messengers brought, and do not accept God's verses which have ever been and shall ever be the conclusive proof as the criterion, then bring what you have if you be truthful. You must bring forth that criterion and proof by which you prove your truth today. By God! You will never be able to do so.

order.why: Imagine the question from another tradition.
Compare accepting the former and rejecting the latter.
Apply the question to the Bab.
Compare similar verses across revelations.
shortened: Say: If ye deny this proof, then by what proof do ye reject the Faith of the Furqan? If ye say they denied God and His verses after they were sent down in truth, ye too have denied their like and their Revealer. What, then, is the difference between you, O company of the deluded?

order.why: Ask what established earlier belief.
shortened: Say: If ye deny these verses, then by what proof have ye believed in all the Prophets and Messengers? Bring it forth if ye be truthful!

order.why: Examine earlier faith in Muhammad.
Bring fairness into inherited belief.
shortened: Say: O people! Be fair before God - if ye deny this Cause which hath dawned from the Supreme Horizon, by what proof can ye establish that which ye possess? Be fair, and be not of the wrongdoers.

order.why: Request evidence for existing claims.
Return to earlier Messengers’ proofs.
shortened: Say: If ye deny these verses, by what proof did ye believe in God's Messengers of old?

order.why: Read consistency within the appeal to fairness.
shortened: Say: O concourse of servants! Be fair before God - if ye deny God's proof and testimony in this Revelation, by what evidence can your own faith be established? Bring it forth, and be not of them that deny. This is a Day wherein the proof calleth aloud and the evidence crieth out.

order.why: Consider sovereignty, proof and evidence together.
Read verses and meanings as context.
shortened: Verily He hath come with the standards of verses and the hosts of meanings. If ye deny Him, by what proof can ye establish what ye possess?

order.why: Ask which book supported earlier faith.
Join power, knowledge and revealed words.
shortened: O people of the earth! Hearken unto My call and then judge fairly in this irrevocable, this wise Cause. If ye deny Me, despite what the hand of My power hath manifested, and what the tongue of My knowledge hath proclaimed, and what the heaven of My will hath revealed, then by what proof can your faith in God, the Lord of the mighty Throne, be established?

order.why: Invite coming forth and judging fairly.
Consider the challenge to Bayan believers.
Read Ali and the recurring proof question.
shortened: O people! This is indeed 'Ali in truth, who hath appeared with such evidence as hath rendered powerless all who are in the heavens and on the earth. He reciteth unto you at every moment from verses of which a single letter surpasseth all things, were ye of them that know. If ye deny them, by what proof do ye uphold your belief in God? Produce it, if ye be truthful!

order.why: Return to the utterance first accepted.
Examine one’s evidence before dismissing another.
Compare proofs in earlier ages.
Consider courage despite general opposition.
Read continuity through the Spirit and Muhammad.
shortened: Say: O people, have mercy upon yourselves and oppose not Him Who hath come to you with the proof of the Spirit, the testimony of Muhammad and the evidences of the Messengers.

order.why: Follow the earlier witnesses and present sovereignty.
shortened: He hath stood between heaven and earth with mighty sovereignty, and there hath appeared from Him the proof of 'Ali, then the evidence of Muhammad, then the testimony of the Spirit, then that which was brought by Him Who conversed with God. Beyond all this, He hath appeared with such sovereignty as no eye in all creation hath witnessed the like thereof, nor the eyes of the angels near unto God.

order.why: Read continuity through the concealed Announcement.
shortened: By God! There hath appeared the proof of 'Ali, then the evidence of Muhammad, then the testimony of the Spirit, then that which the Interlocutor brought from the Sinai of God through this Announcement which was inscribed by the Pen of God in the mystery of the line, concealed from the gaze of the hypocrites.

order.why: Retain the appeal concerning prophetic proofs.
shortened: Say: Fear ye God, and reject not Him Who hath come to you with the proofs of the Prophets and with that whereof the eye of creation hath seen no likeness.

order.why: Join scriptural continuity with fairness.
Consider implications of rejecting a later Messenger.
shortened: Whoso denieth Him hath denied the Messengers of God in the past, disputed His signs, and disbelieved in His proof.

order.why: Read the Bab’s sufficiently supported claim criterion.
Examine Abraham’s community and teachings.
shortened: Behold what a power it was that enabled an emigrant to establish such a family, to found such a nation, and to promulgate such teachings. Now, can anyone claim that all this was purely fortuitous? We must be fair: Was this Man an Educator or not?

order.why: Compare Moses’ circumstances and achievement.
shortened: Now, how could a man who was a stammerer, who had been brought up in the house of Pharaoh, who was known among men as a murderer, and who out of fear had long been a fugitive and a shepherd, establish in the world so mighty a Cause that the wisest philosophers of the earth would be incapable of producing a thousandth part thereof? This is clearly an extraordinary feat.
No: Were He not assisted by a divine power, He would never have been able to carry out such a mighty task. These are arguments that none can deny.

order.why: Consider the Bab as universal Educator.
shortened: The manifestation of such marvellous signs and mighty undertakings, the influence exerted upon the thoughts and minds of the people, the laying of the foundations of progress, and the establishment of the prerequisites of success and prosperity by a young merchant constitute the greatest proof that He was a universal Educator---a fact that no fair-minded person would ever hesitate to acknowledge.

order.why: Read ordinary occupations and divine confirmation.
shortened: The Greater Peter, known as Simon the Pure, was outwardly a dyer, and Noah the Pure was outwardly a carpenter. When they received divine confirmation, one saved a people from the Most Great Flood and the other illumined a world with the lights of guidance.

order.why: Examine advance from imprisonment.
shortened: Now, since that Luminary of truth has set, all stand in need of proofs, and so we have been occupied with providing rational proofs. Let us mention another, and this undeniable proof should alone suffice any fair-minded soul: It is that this illustrious Being advanced His Cause from within the Most Great Prison, whence His light shone forth, His fame encircled the globe, and the word of His glory reached both East and West. To this day such a thing has never come to pass, if the matter be examined with fairness.

order.why: Ask what exceeds ordinary human ability.
shortened: Say: The Cause of God is more manifest than to need proof or evidence, for in all times and ages there hath appeared that which transcendeth human capacity. Therefore, the excuse of those who hesitate is unacceptable before God. Were people to adorn themselves with fairness, all would acknowledge that the divine testimony and proof of the All-Glorious, the Self-Subsisting, hath appeared in its essence.

order.why: Bring together the Tablet of the Signs.
shortened: Among His signs is His being manifest, being seen by all, standing as His own proof, and His presence among witnesses in every region, among peoples who fell upon Him even as wolves, and compassed Him about from every side.
Among His signs is His withstanding powerful nations and all-conquering states, and a host of enemies thirsting for His blood, intent at every moment upon His ruin, wheresoever He might be.

Another of His signs is the marvel of His discourse, the eloquence of His utterance, the rapidity with which His Writings were revealed, His words of wisdom, His verses, His epistles, His communes, His unfolding of the Qur'an, both the abstruse verses thereof and the clear.

order.why: Distinguish historical account from argument.
shortened: Were these to be discussed in detail it would conduce to prolixity, and our object is the statement of history, not of arguments for believing or rejecting; but of some of the replies the gist is this: that they held the Proof as supreme, and the evidence as outweighing traditions, considering the former as the root and the latter as the branch, and saying, "If the branch agree not with the root it serves not as an argument and is unworthy of reliance; for the reported consequence has no right to oppose itself to the established principle, and cannot argue against it."

order.why: Compare the reported fourfold approach.
shortened: Whenever the Holy Manifestations of God appear in this world they establish their validity with certain proofs. One of their proofs is the prophecies given by former Manifestations. The second is the wonderful traces which emanate from their personality. The third proof is their own deeds. The fourth proof is their teachings.

order.why: Read its formulation with creative words.
shortened: When the prophets of God appear upon this earth, their validity is established by means of certain proofs. One of the proofs is through the fulfillment of former prophecies, the second proofs are their creative words and phrases which salute the hearts of humanity, the third are their deeds and the fourth are their teachings.

order.why: Acknowledge the reported variety of proofs.
Hear the written account of that abundance.
shortened: As to the matter of proof, it hath appeared with the brilliance of the sun at high noon and become renowned throughout all regions. Indeed, I am at a loss to determine which of the manifest proofs, clear evidences, and conclusive arguments that have appeared in this mighty Dispensation and noble age I should mention to thee. Shall I speak of the purified Scriptures and perfected Books which have rendered all the eloquent ones and learned ones on earth powerless, or shall I tell thee of the evident might of Truth, His resplendent power and His triumphant glory which have encompassed all horizons?

order.why: Consider reported preservation amidst opponents.
shortened: In former dispensations, the proof of the Manifestation of God was perfect, but now it is more than perfect. The most wonderful event in this Revelation, was the protection of the Blessed Perfection while under the claws of the Shah of Persia and the Sultan of Turkey. His safeguard was like unto the safeguard of a blessed nightingale surrounded by a thousand eagles or an innocent lamp encircled by a hundred thousand wolves, or a small ark encompassed by furious and raging waves.

order.why: Read reported growth through persecution.
shortened: Conversely, one of the miracles of the Word of God and manifest signs of those who claim to be from God is that despite the oppression of enemies and killing, torture and tribulation, their Cause grows more influential day by day. Abasement becomes the cause of glory, captivity and imprisonment takes on the decree of freedom and deliverance.

order.why: Keep successive exiles and increased strength.
Read courage under suffering.
Consider testimony of those who sacrificed.
shortened: Among the proofs was the fact that blessed souls who believed and sacrificed their lives were from among the most prominent and distinguished people of the nation, both clergy and others. And so forth. All conversations were presentations of proof and evidence.

order.why: Keep the particular Sacrifice in context.
shortened: By the Sun of the horizon of sanctity! If thou wouldst reflect upon the circumstances of the Sacrifice mentioned in thy letter concerning the people of Za, this same would constitute the greatest proof for thee and all peoples.

order.why: Read endurance and worlds beyond this life.
shortened: If thou wouldst reflect upon the deeds of the Prophets, thou wouldst bear witness with absolute certitude that there are worlds besides this world. The philosophers of the earth, as revealed in the Tablet of Wisdom by the Supreme Pen, have mostly acknowledged and accepted what was revealed in the divine Books.
Now if such souls had considered divine worlds to be limited to this earthly life, they would never have surrendered themselves to their enemies nor endured unprecedented trials and tribulations.

order.why: Remember opposition despite signs.
shortened: The Manifestations of God have ever appeared with conclusive proofs and clear and evident testimonies, and yet in every Dispensation there hath been visited upon these sacred Temples that which the pen is powerless to recount.

order.why: Preserve the questions about steadfastness.
Read the reported offer to divines.
Keep testimony of friends and opponents attributed.
Read all conditions characterized as miracles.
shortened: If thou seekest proof, praise be to God that the horizons are illumined by the lamp of divine evidence. All the conditions of the Blessed Beauty were miracles.

order.why: Examine literal expectations as a barrier.
Recall the demands made of Muhammad.
shortened: Now consider those heedless souls who demanded that He cause a spring to gush forth in the land of Batha, or manifest for them a house of gold, or ascend to heaven before their eyes and bring a book they could read, or produce a garden with date palms and grapes, or come with God, exalted be His glory, and a company of angels.

order.why: Study the Tablets to the Kings.
shortened: The warnings of the Blessed Beauty to the kings of the earth are utterly clear, without interpretation, and need no explanation. The Tablets to the Kings are sufficient and complete proof of the divine supernatural power. Study the Tablets to the Kings, consider carefully the severe addresses and observe the mighty warnings.

order.why: Keep interreligious prophecy claims attributed.
shortened: As to the Manifestation (Baha'u'llah) all the religious books in the world bear witness to Him. The Magis have resisted the Mohammedans for nearly 1,400 years, refusing to accept Mohammedanism, and suffered great persecutions. They accept and believe in the manifestation (Baha'u'llah) because of the prophecies of their books. The Jews would not accept Christ, but, because they see their Bible prophecies literally fulfilled, they are becoming believers in great numbers.

order.why: Read the encouragement to investigate fulfillment.
shortened: Now as to the coming of the great Master. His appearance [one or two words have been scratched off the page] is dependent upon the realization of certain conditions. Investigate the reality and in whomsoever these conditions are fulfilled, know ye of a certainty that he is the Great Master.

order.why: Value investigating earlier books.
shortened: Raise both hands in thanksgiving to the threshold of the One God, offer praise and glory, and render laudation and gratitude that you have been confirmed and assisted with such a bounty - that you have extracted from ancient books decisive proofs, clear evidences and manifest arguments establishing the truth of the Great Announcement.

order.why: Read the focus on Bab and Bahaullah.
Consider the declaration of the Promised One.
shortened: Say: Yea, by My life! This is He Who was promised in the Scriptures and Tablets. If this be Baha's crime, what sayest thou of Him Who declared "Verily I am God from time immemorial"?

order.why: Keep Scriptures and Tablets together.
Read prior disclosure as a source assertion.
shortened: Nay more: whatsoever hath come to pass upon the earth, and whatsoever shall come to pass, hath already proceeded and flowed from the Divine Pen, in such wise that no fair-minded soul can deny it; and notwithstanding, they have arisen to turn away. What proof is greater than this? What evidence more exalted than that which hath been mentioned?

order.why: Compare the staff and the Pen.
Read Tablets alongside earlier prophetic trials.
Keep the apocalyptic reply in context.
shortened: As to what thou hast written concerning the manifestation of the Cause and the completion of the proof, know thou that the proof hath been completed, the heavenly table hath descended, the earth hath been cleft asunder, the heaven hath been split, the mountains have been scattered, the trees have been uprooted, the seas have been frozen, the path hath been laid, the balance hath been set up, the trumpet hath been blown, the door hath been knocked, the hosts have been arrayed, the inevitable hour hath come to pass, the tribes have been shaken, the bugle hath sounded, and the voice of the trumpet hath been raised, when this most exalted Word was sent down from the Most Exalted Pen: My glory and grandeur bear witness that this is not the day for questions.

order.why: Preserve the particular House in Fars criterion.
Retain recording statements for judgment.
Keep the Bab’s specific attributes of the Bearer.
Preserve the reference and elemental exposition.
Retain the promise of continuing creation.
Keep the testimony to divine unity.
Read creation, command and completed proof.
shortened: His is the creation and the command. There is none other God but Him. Say: All are His worshippers. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Verily, the verses are from Him, a proof unto all who dwell in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and all that lieth between them, and through them are ye all created.
Say: This is a proof that hath been completed in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, then throughout the worlds.

order.why: Consider each Messenger’s token.
Connect succession with drawing people nearer.
Follow continuity toward the Spirit.
Read signs as mercy amid varied capacities.
Notice inclusion across age and sex.
shortened: He hath manifested His beauty with such a proof as hath rendered all created things powerless, and through it His evidence hath been perfected, His proof completed, and His testimony hath shone forth unto all in the kingdom, whether female or male, whether young or old.

order.why: Read the call without recompense.
Connect proof with guidance and nearness.
shortened: Praise be to God Who sent down the Proof to His servants, made manifest to them the Way, and caused them to know the Dawning-Place of His Cause, the Rising-Point of His verses, the Source of His laws, and the Recipient of His knowledge - He Who stood before all faces and spoke that which draweth the servants nigh unto the court of His glory and the horizon of His Cause.

order.why: Keep the signs’ guiding purpose.
shortened: Say: He hath come with the truth, with signs from His presence, that He might guide you to His resplendent horizon.

order.why: Join wisdom’s fruits and revealed proof.
Read transformed perception as testimony.
Consider inward movement through its effects.
shortened: Then, at that time, the radiance of that widespread effulgence will descend upon thee successively, and that motion rendered thee by the Holy Spirit will make thee dispense with any other strong evidence that leadeth to the appearance of this Light, because the greatest and strongest proof for showing the abundance of the Spirit to the bodies is the very appearance of its power and influence in those bodies. Think deeply of this in order to know the reality of my explanation and demonstration.

order.why: Read rending veils beside cleaving the sun.
shortened: Today the horizons of the hearts of the friends are illumined by the lights of the luminous Orb of Revelation and are set aflame by the ardor of Divine love. The light is shining forth, the fire is manifest, power is revealed, and might is resplendent. By the life of God! To rend the veils of names and to sunder them seemeth, in this sight, greater than the cleaving of the moon. I swear by the lights of His countenance: in this Revelation the cleaving of the sun is beheld, could ye but know it.

order.why: Look within horizons and ourselves.
Read the sight imagery with omissions preserved.
shortened: O servants of God! The signs of divine power are evident in all things like the sun, but the blind ones say "Where is this manifest light and where is this proof and where is this path?"
Otherwise, if there were even a particle of sight, one would witness the greatest signs and observe all things as clear proof of the existence of the Glorious Lord.

order.why: Attend to varied senses of recognition.
shortened: Is there one endowed with the sense of smell who can inhale the fragrance of God from His most exalted Word? Is there one possessed of sight who can behold My luminous countenance? Is there one with hearing who can hear My most sweet call? Is there one with a heart who can detect My pervading fragrance between the heavens and the earth?

order.why: Receive the invitation to see and hear.
shortened: Say: The verses We have revealed are as numerous as those which, in the preceding Revelation, were sent down upon the Bab. Let him that doubteth the words which the Spirit of God hath spoken seek the court of Our presence and hear Our divinely-revealed verses, and be an eye-witness of the clear proof of Our claim.

order.why: Pause over Revelation’s mightiness.
Read the appeal to momentary fairness.
Compare a claimed greater proof fairly.
shortened: And when thou hast recited them unto them say: O people! If ye possess a proof greater than this, bring it forth and be not of those who tarry.
O people! Be fair and deny not this Dayspring which hath shone forth upon the horizons with the lights of God, the Sovereign, the Dawning, the Mighty, the Luminous.

order.why: Weigh possessions against what has appeared.
Keep the invitation to bring greater proof.
shortened: If ye possess that which can equal these fragrances sent forth by the Mighty, the Wondrous One, or a proof greater than what We have, then bring it forth and tarry not, O people, and be not of them that slumber.

order.why: Read the Balance beyond prior possessions.
Retain the concise appeal to fairness.
shortened: Say: Be fair, O people of the earth, concerning this Cause at whose appearance bodies and souls were made to tremble.

order.why: Consider opposition as a barrier to perception.
Read expectations of another revelation as a barrier.
Keep seeing and disobeying together.
Examine longing followed by refusal.
shortened: Say: O people! If ye believed in God before, how is it that ye believe not in Him around Whom circle the angels of the highest heaven? Say: Did ye not yearn for Him in the nights and at dawn? Yet when He came unto you with clear signs, ye turned away from His beauty.

order.why: Read recognition through the rising sun.
shortened: Behold what hath appeared in truth, then be fair, and be not of those who said "God is our Lord," but when He came from the horizon of might they said "This is naught but a lying impostor." The trumpet hath been sounded in truth, yet the people are in doubt and strife. Say: Look ye, look ye, for the Sun hath risen from the horizon of proof.

order.why: Keep the source’s portrayal of resistance.
Read heedlessness beside stated proofs.
shortened: If thou hast believed in God, why hast thou turned away from Him Who hath come unto thee with that wherewith came the Prophets and Messengers? By God! He hath come with God's proofs and His evidence, but most of the people are heedless.

order.why: Turn from fancies toward utterance.
Keep rising evidence amid error.
shortened: The proof hath appeared and the sun of evidence hath shone forth from the horizon of possibility, yet the people are in grievous error.

order.why: Read the stated loss of turning away.
Retain signs distinguishing false claims.
shortened: And when God knew that some people would claim the station of Lordship in the temple of servitude without deserving it, God created for its people signs that would indicate its true possessor and distinguish between truth and falsehood.

order.why: Keep the Book’s claim of inimitability.
Imagine utterance’s ocean across horizons.
Hear the attractive yet unheard call.
shortened: Glorified be He Who hath appeared with the truth with all the signs and hath spoken between earth and heaven with a call whereby the hearts of the Concourse on High were attracted, yet most of the people hear not.

order.why: Read the address to Bayan believers.
shortened: Say: O people of the Bayan! This, verily, is the Proof that hath shone forth from the horizon of the All-Merciful with power and sovereignty.

order.why: Connect remembrance, utterance and exposition.
Retain the Youth’s mighty signs.
shortened: Say: O people! Verily, He is the Youth of God amongst you, Who hath come unto you with the truth, with mighty signs.

order.why: Read personified proof and testimony.
Keep the claim concerning one letter.
shortened: Say: O people! This is in truth Husayn Who hath come to you with verses, a single letter of which all who are in the heavens and on earth cannot equal, did ye but know.

order.why: Retain the declaration of sovereignty.
shortened: Say: Verily, He is the One Who hath appeared, and He is the One Who hath come with the truth, with a sovereignty that hath subdued all who are in the heavens and on earth.

order.why: Read proof alongside completed favor.
Keep the appeal against opposing the signs.
Preserve the reference to a prayer’s opening.
shortened: What proof could be greater than this, and what evidence mightier than this station? Observe how this blessed word adorns the opening of the prayer.

order.why: Read power filling the horizons.
Return to proof surrounding the Manifestation.
Hear the invitation to seekers of proof.
shortened: Say: O people! If ye desire verses, they have been sent down in truth, and if ye seek clear proofs, they have appeared from this visible horizon.

order.why: Argues for humanity’s need of a universal educator through the analogy of an army’s commander.
Connect proof with arising to assist.
Retain the question about denial’s basis.
shortened: Were one possessed of insight, he would cry out between earth and heaven saying: "O people! By what proof have ye denied this Beauty Who hath dawned from the horizon of holiness with sovereignty and power?

order.why: Distinguish power, attributes and signs.
Read the repeated questions about doubt.
shortened: Say: Is there any doubt concerning Him, or concerning the verses revealed unto Him, or concerning His power which hath encompassed all worlds? Say: This is from the appearance of that which the eye of creation hath never witnessed its like, and whoso denieth it hath disbelieved in God and His Messengers, then in Him Who came unto you with mighty sovereignty.

order.why: Keep one letter beside encompassing power.
shortened: Say: Is there any doubt about God, or about His power which hath encompassed all created things, or about His signs, one letter of which all that can be counted cannot equal?

order.why: Receive the prayer’s testimony to mysteries.
Read the personified witnesses.
Retain verses as a proof.
Keep the testimony to the Bab.
shortened: And that 'Ali before Nabil is the Manifestation of His Self to all who are in the heavens and on earth, and He hath sent Him with a proof that confoundeth the minds of the wise and the hearts of them that are near unto God.

order.why: Read the opened gate and Book.
Consider verses across the world.
shortened: If the proof be verses, verily they have filled the world, and if it be evidences, verily they have shone forth from the horizon of the Will of the Lord of Eternity.

order.why: Let sunlight-like clarity stand briefly.
shortened: Though the Cause is mighty indeed, yet its proof and testimony are seen to be clearer than the light of the sun.

order.why: Retain the proclamation of this Day.
shortened: Say: This is the Day wherein verses have been sent down and clear proofs have been made manifest.

order.why: Keep one word’s stated sublimity.
shortened: Should He utter but one word, verily it would be more sublime than all that hath been uttered by the tongues from time immemorial. He seeth and witnesseth, and He, verily, is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

order.why: Read proofs circling the Evidence.
shortened: The proofs have circled round My proof, and the evidences round My transcendent and mighty and impregnable Evidence.

order.why: Retain evidence before His face.
Compare testimony with incomprehension.
Join proof to the unsealed wine.
shortened: Say: O people! If you desire verses, they have indeed encompassed all directions, and if you desire proofs, they have verily appeared through the truth, and if you desire the choice sealed wine, by God, its seal has been broken by the finger of divine power from God, the Lord of all being.

order.why: Keep fairness within recognition.
Retain sovereignty beyond opposing hosts.
shortened: Verily He hath appeared with the truth with such sovereignty as no hosts of the heavens and earth can withstand.

order.why: Read the submission of evidence.
shortened: Every proof hath bowed down before the proof of God, the Lord of all worlds, and every evidence hath submitted to the evidence of God, the Lord of the mighty throne.

order.why: Connect unveiling with certitude.
shortened: We have rent asunder the veils and sent down the verses, that perchance the people may attain certitude through the meeting with their Lord.

order.why: Hear the summons to the path.
Keep the repeated assurance about doubt.
shortened: Is there any doubt concerning Him? Nay, by His own Self, the Truth! Is there any uncertainty about Him? Nay, by His own Self, the All-Bountiful!

order.why: Retain the All-Informed’s proclamation.
shortened: By God! The All-Informed hath proclaimed My Manifestation, and the All-Knowing crieth out before My luminous countenance.

order.why: Receive praise for revealed evidence.
shortened: Glorified is He Who hath sent down the verses and made manifest the clear evidences for people who know.

order.why: Read wine within the declaration of kingdom.
shortened: Praise be to God Who hath broken the seal of the choice Wine with the finger of power and hath caused to descend from the heaven of utterance that whereby all things have proclaimed: "The Kingdom belongeth to Him Who hath appeared with the truth with such conclusive proof as hath caused all necks to bow down."

order.why: Keep continuing proof and its obstruction.
shortened: Even this much that has been mentioned was solely to establish proof, so that they might realize at least this much - that this earth will never be devoid of a manifest proof, and what prevents its manifestation and appearance in this age and era are the evil souls of the people.

order.why: Read the brief assurance of evidence.
Distinguish opposing books from examining proof.
shortened: Consider how in the days of the Prophet--peace be upon Him--it was even more severe than this. Therefore these books are of no importance. Rather, importance lieth in the proof and evidence. Since the proof is brilliant, all these books are but vain imaginings.

order.why: Turn toward instruction for younger believers.
Include girls’ education and evidence.
Consider sustained gatherings for learning.
shortened: Today the teaching of the Faith is the mightiest foundation, and the acquisition of proofs and arguments is obligatory, and knowledge of conclusive evidences for the appearance of the manifest Light is necessary. The gathering thou hast arranged brought much joy and gladness to the heart of 'Abdu'l-Baha. Surely thou wilt carry forward with effort, persistence and steadfastness so that, God willing, through the divine breaths souls may be educated who will each become a shining lamp in the gathering of divine knowledge. This matter is very important and incumbent upon all.

order.why: Keep the encouragement to remember proofs.
shortened: Told of the study of the Ighan in the Wednesday night meetings in Washington, his comment was, "Very good! Very good! It is very good to memorize the logical points and the proofs of the Holy Books. Those proofs and evidences which establish the fact that Baha'u'llah is the fulfilment of the Promises of the Holy Books. These proofs ought to be collected and memorized. As soon as someone will ask you--What are your proofs?--you may cry out at the top of your voice and say: 'Here they are!'"

order.why: Join rational and traditional evidence.
Read gatherings as reasoned inquiry.
shortened: It is my hope that from day to day your gatherings will grow and flourish, and that those who are seeking after truth will hearken therein to reasoned arguments and conclusive proofs.

order.why: Keep meetings’ educational purpose.
shortened: In these meetings the believers and maid-servants of the Merciful must proclaim the proofs and arguments and explain the signs of the appearance of the Beauty of Abha-May my life by a sacrifice to the beloved ones!

But the fundamental principle of the establishment of spiritual meetings is for the sake of teaching and delivering the Truth so that those souls who are present may become informed of the Divine Evidences and Proofs.

order.why: Join conduct with explaining arguments.
Receive encouragement to an investigator.
Read the brief response to objectors.
shortened: Indeed, through the power of proof you silence the objectors until the spiritual realities and meanings become manifest and evident.

order.why: Preserve the interview without supplying missing arguments.
Keep the exchange with a rabbi attributed.
Retain the missionaries’ question without inventing an answer.
Return to gratitude despite opposition.
shortened: Let not the words of those who have disbelieved in God grieve thee. Glorify the praise of thy Lord and say: Praise be unto Thee, O Thou Who hast made Thyself known unto me and hast sent unto me that whereby the dead are quickened.

order.why: Close linked readings with gladdening hearts.
shortened: It is incumbent upon thee to gladden hearts and bring joy to souls and unite the word among the loved ones and show love toward all creation and manifest great kindness toward those who have walked the straight path, and to recite the verses and set forth proofs and evidences for the appearance of the Kingdom of God in this great century.

order.why: Read the Prophets’ testimony as a balance.
Preserve investigation of life and history.
Return to beneficent accomplishment.
Close with the supplied tree and fruits image.

questions: What different kinds of evidence do these passages offer, and how might they illuminate or challenge one another?
How could we investigate the claim that a Manifestation educates humanity while also taking seriously the misuse of religion by its professed followers?
What standards do we apply to traditions we already accept, and what might change if we applied those standards consistently to unfamiliar claims?
How do the readings distinguish recognition of a Person, examination of teachings, and reports of extraordinary events?
What do the Gospel’s fruits and the Qur’an’s challenge concerning its own text invite us to consider about religious evidence?
How might a conversation about proofs remain both intellectually searching and a source of kindness, learning, and unity?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 7:15–20 · Knowing a tree by its fruits
references.note: Jesus warns against deceptive prophetic appearances and directs attention to the fruit a tree bears. Compare this image with the compilation’s accounts of education, conduct, and the transformation of human lives. What would careful attention to such fruits involve across different places and generations?

references.label: 2 · Qur’an 17:88 · The challenge of the revealed Word
references.note: This verse declares that humans and jinn together could not produce the like of the Qur’an, even by assisting one another. Read the parallel translations beside the Báb’s and Bahá’u’lláh’s arguments concerning revealed verses. Consider how a scriptural claim becomes a criterion of recognition, and what consistent use of that criterion would require.

subjects.displayTitle: A pure heart: seeing clearly and serving freely
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh’s first counsel is to possess a pure, kindly and radiant heart, and He calls it a sovereignty no one can take away. Purity here is not pallor or withdrawal. It means a heart cleared of malice, envy and prejudice, a tongue that does not deceive, and a hand that will not reach for a neighbour’s property even in hunger. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá presses the question deeper, into motive: the help that quietly remembers it was given loses its worth at the moment the thought occurs. The polished mirror runs through His teaching as the picture of what a cleansed heart becomes, able to receive light and give it back, and He insists that a grown person can win a child’s simplicity through strength of understanding rather than innocence. Psalm 24 joins clean hands to a pure heart and truthful speech, and the Dhammapada traces every word and act to the mind behind it. The way onward leads through the soul as a mirror, through goodly deeds that make sincerity visible, and through prayer for a heart kept clean.
subjects.arc: Begin with kindness and freedom from prejudice; examine motives through concrete conduct; explore the mirror and mature simplicity; investigate purity as a condition of understanding; follow prayer and remembrance into steadfast, generous service.

order.why: Open with the pure, kindly and radiant heart.
Define defilement through harm and self-admiration.
shortened: Say: O children of dust! He Who is the Spirit of Purity saith: In this glorious Day whatsoever can purge you from defilement and ensure your peace and tranquillity, that indeed is the Straight Path, the Path that leadeth unto Me. To be purged from defilement is to be cleansed of that which is injurious to man and detracteth from his high station--among which is to take undue pleasure in one's own words and deeds, notwithstanding their unworthiness.

order.why: Explicitly separate purity of heart from racial color.
shortened: A man's heart may be pure and white though his outer skin be black; or his heart be dark and sinful though his racial color is white. The character and purity of the heart is of all importance. The heart illumined by the light of God is nearest and dearest to God, and inasmuch as God has endowed man with such favor that he is called the image of God, this is truly a supreme perfection of attainment, a divine station which is not to be sacrificed by the mere accident of color.

order.why: Name hatred and malice as the thorns.
shortened: Illumine and hallow your hearts; let them not be profaned by the thorns of hate or the thistles of malice.

order.why: Connect cleansing prejudice with love across every community.
shortened: Abstract yourselves from these imaginations and cleanse and polish the mirrors of your hearts form the dross of these ignorant prejudices - thus you may become real kind and loving to the world of humanity, serving mankind with faithfulness and entertaining not the least trace of ill-feeling against the individual members of any nation, any religion, any community, any race and any country.

order.why: Join freedom from rancor with joyful fellowship.
shortened: Blessed is the servant who hath cast away vain desire and taken unto himself the fear of God, and hath purified his heart from all rancor and hatred, and who associateth with all people in a spirit of fragrant joy.

order.why: Name conflict, corruption and hatred as obstacles.
Bring envy into the work of the heart.
shortened: Purify your hearts from envy and hatred that ye may meet your Lord, the All-Merciful, with sanctified hearts.

order.why: Read purification as preparation to serve all.
shortened: By the command of God, exalted be His glory, they have arisen to serve all, their hearts sanctified and purified from rancor, hatred, doubts, idle fancies, selfish desires and vain imaginings.

order.why: Join pure hearts with justice against oppression.
shortened: I hope you will always avoid tyranny and oppression, and that you will always uphold and practice justice towards all men and keep your hearts pure.

order.why: Test purity through respect for another’s property.
shortened: Verily I say: Incline your ears to My sweet voice, and sanctify yourselves from the defilement of your evil passions and corrupt desires. They who dwell within the tabernacle of God, and are established upon the seats of everlasting glory, will refuse, though they be dying of hunger, to stretch their hands and seize unlawfully the property of their neighbor, however vile and worthless he may be.

order.why: Connect sincerity with the public interest.
shortened: Sincerity is the foundation-stone of faith. That is, a religious individual must disregard his personal desires and seek in whatever way he can wholeheartedly to serve the public interest; and it is impossible for a human being to turn aside from his own selfish advantages and sacrifice his own good for the good of the community except through true religious faith.

order.why: Keep the welfare of all as the aim.
shortened: But I bear witness regarding you that you have no purpose save the good-pleasure of God, no desire save the welfare of all.

order.why: Read thoughtfulness toward others as essential conduct.
Imagine truthful and trustworthy relationships.
Join inward stability with refusing corruption.
shortened: Be ye pure in heart before God such that your feet slip not and your souls be not troubled.

Further do I counsel you not to spread corruption in the earth and to be God's trusted ones among His servants, such that the signs of sanctity may appear from your faces and the lights of detachment from your temples.

order.why: Read trustworthiness beside godliness.
Let truthfulness illuminate the whole person.
Connect truthful speech, sincerity and freedom from guile.
shortened: Adorn your temples with the robes of detachment, and your tongues with truthfulness, and your hearts with sincerity, then make your breasts free from all deceit and guile and doubt.

order.why: Keep the reported consistency of private and public purity.
Connect purity with character visible among all communities.
shortened: This is impossible unless we purify the hem of sanctification and illumine the face of morality, such that we shine like the sun among all communities and move like banners on the hills of nations from the breeze of providence.

order.why: Examine intention beneath an apparently good action.
shortened: The third virtue of humanity is goodly intention, which is the foundation of all good deeds. Some seekers after truth have held intention to be superior to action, for a goodly intention is absolute light and is entirely sanctified from the least trace of malice, scheming, or deception. Now, one can perform an action which appears to be righteous but which is in reality prompted by self-interest.

order.why: Confront the searching example of generosity without a claim.
Read charity without an expectation of return.
shortened: If you serve someone, do not allow this hypocrisy to enter your heart, so that your service and your charity may be true to God, and its effects more enduring. As far as you can, you must be charitable without the slightest hint of hypocrisy and without any expectation of result or reward.

order.why: Consider how a motive changes even a small deed or word.
shortened: Even the smallest of deeds could lead to manifest loss in this day if it is not performed for the sake of God; even the barest word is capable of causing fires to blaze if uttered without motives that are purely for the sake of God.

order.why: Join pure intention with work founded on truth.
shortened: The intention must be pure and the work must be founded on truth. This is the truth, and after truth there is nothing but clear error.

order.why: Examine service for traces of private ambition.
Read motive supported by actual deeds.
shortened: The days when idle worship was deemed sufficient are ended. The time is come when naught but the purest motive, supported by deeds of stainless purity, can ascend to the throne of the Most High and be acceptable unto Him.

order.why: Bring the Hidden Words’ counsel into daily life.
shortened: Holy words and pure and goodly deeds ascend unto the heaven of celestial glory. Strive that your deeds may be cleansed from the dust of self and hypocrisy and find favor at the court of glory; for ere long the assayers of mankind shall, in the holy presence of the Adored One, accept naught but absolute virtue and deeds of stainless purity.

order.why: Consider the value of one pure deed.
shortened: Repeatedly hath this exalted word been uttered by the Lord of all being: One pure deed will cause the essence of earth to transcend the heavens and reach the Dayspring of Revelation. O people of God! Strive! O people of God! Endeavor! that perchance the idols of self and desire may be destroyed through the power of detachment, and godliness may be established upon its throne.

order.why: Keep the single deed performed for God’s sake.
shortened: The fragrance of a single deed performed purely for His sake in the Day of God is reckoned as the chief of deeds before God and is recorded by the Most Exalted Pen.

order.why: Join goodly words with pure deeds.
shortened: Nothing but pure deeds and goodly words have ever been or shall ever be worthy of God's threshold.

order.why: Read sincerity as a fragrance of conduct.
shortened: Then adorn your deeds with the ornament of sanctity, that the fragrance of sincerity may waft from you amongst all servants.

order.why: Consider how conduct can obscure a religious message.
Read virtue and action as the assayers’ concern.
Connect discernment of actions with their purity.
shortened: Say: It behoveth every one that holdeth fast to the hem of Our Robe to be untainted by anything from which the Concourse on high may be averse.
We verily behold your actions. If We perceive from them the sweet smelling savor of purity and holiness, We will most certainly bless you.

order.why: Read sanctified conduct as true victory.
shortened: Sanctify your souls and your deeds in such wise that all atoms shall testify to your sanctification, and this verily is the true victory, would that ye might know.

order.why: Consider deeds that attract hearts.
shortened: Say: O people! Purify your deeds and sanctify your souls, that there may appear from you that whereby the hearts of all men shall be attracted.

order.why: Ask how conduct exalts other people.
shortened: We counsel the loved ones of God to purify and sanctify themselves, and to perform such deeds as will cause the exaltation of His servants.

order.why: Imagine an action’s influence spreading outward.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath arisen to act in such wise that the fragrance of sanctity hath been wafted therefrom throughout the world. We testify that he is among the faithful and the sincere ones.

order.why: Connect intention with reformation.
shortened: Assuredly when intention becomes pure, the effulgences of the light of reformation become manifest and evident.

order.why: Read sincerity within the manner of service.
Attend to the essence of intention.
Join sincerity with exertion.
shortened: Therefore, strive in sincerity of intention and exertion of effort so that like a magnet you may attract divine confirmations.

order.why: Allow effort and its results time to develop.
shortened: One must not look to the beginning of matters - one must strive in affairs with pure intention and ultimately await the results.

order.why: Read encouragement concerning righteous motives.
shortened: Indeed, thou hast a pure intention and a radiant heart. Rest assured that sincere intentions and righteous motives in themselves attract divine confirmation and draw the assistance of the Glorious Lord.

order.why: Connect pure intention with joyful service.
shortened: Be certain that your pure intention will definitely yield results and divine confirmations will surely be attained.
Whether I am present or absent, I am with you and seek your success so that with a pure heart and joyous soul you may succeed in serving the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Keep the assurance concerning work for God.
shortened: Praise be to God, since the intention is for God's sake, be assured, and God will establish the truth through His words.

order.why: Seek an intention made visible through action.
shortened: May you be assisted to achieve that which will make your pure intention and turning to truth manifest and evident like the sun.

order.why: Retain the tribute to a faithful friend.
shortened: What can I write of the pure intentions, the supreme endeavor, the worship of truth, and the servitude at the threshold of oneness of that faithful friend who is in the utmost joy and delight.

order.why: Read the reported testimony to a community’s aim.
shortened: Your hearts are pure. I bear witness that you have no other aim but that which is good. Your aim is to serve the Kingdom of GOD.

order.why: Imagine sincerity perceptible to others.
shortened: How excellent is the state of those souls who in this day manifest complete sincerity, such that every possessor of spiritual sense can detect from them the fragrance of the sanctified Garment of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Introduce the mirror polished by love and detachment.
shortened: A pure heart is as a mirror; cleanse it with the burnish of love and severance from all save God, that the true sun may shine therein and the eternal morning dawn.

order.why: Distinguish the reflecting mirror from the source of light.
shortened: Souls are like unto mirrors, and the bounty of God is like unto the sun. When the mirrors pass beyond all coloring and attain purity and polish, and are confronted with the sun, they will reflect in full perfection its light and glory. In this condition one should not consider the mirror, but the power of the light of the sun, which hath penetrated the mirror, making it a reflector of the heavenly glory.

order.why: Connects purity and detachment with reflecting spiritual light and receiving confirmation.
Make polishing the mirror a continuing responsibility.
shortened: The most important thing is to polish the mirrors of hearts in order that they may become illumined and receptive of the divine light.

Therefore, our duty lies in seeking to polish the mirrors of our hearts in order that we shall become reflectors of that light and recipients of the divine bounties which may be fully revealed through them.

order.why: Connect reflected love with the mirror’s clearness.
Read hearts as mirrors of divine attributes.
shortened: Ye are the mirrors of My attributes - polish your hearts from the rust of vain imaginings.

order.why: Let received light illuminate surrounding people.
Compare a polished instrument’s capacity to warm hearts.
Explore hearts that reflect one another.
shortened: When man's soul is rarified and cleansed, spiritual links are established, and from these bonds sensations felt by the heart are produced. The human heart resembleth a mirror. When this is purified human hearts are attuned and reflect one another, and thus spiritual emotions are generated.

order.why: Read the reported conditions for spiritual communication.
shortened: A clear mind, a pure heart and a concentrated attention are the requisites for that spiritual inter-communication.
Like unto a mirror, man's heart and mind must be purified, clarified and polished.

order.why: Keep the personal letter’s image of transcending distance.
Read the address to a photographer through its visual analogy.
Consider the world-revealing cup as the pure heart.
Entrust the sealed secret to that mirror.
Read the face as the heart’s mirror.
Keep the personal response to a photograph attributed.
Consider capacity through the clearer mirror.
shortened: Capacity, worth (or merit) and ability, are necessary, for the clearer and purer the mirror is, the lights of the Sun are more manifest thereon.

order.why: Read the reported account of spiritual capacity.
Hear the mirror image addressed to children.
Distinguish innocent simplicity from mature simplicity.
shortened: The hearts of all children are of the utmost purity. They are mirrors upon which no dust has fallen. But this purity is on account of weakness and innocence, not on account of any strength and testing, for as this is the early period of their childhood, their hearts and minds are unsullied by the world.

This is on account of the child's weakness, whereas the man becomes pure through his strength. Through the power of intelligence he becomes simple; through the great power of reason and understanding and not through the power of weakness he becomes sincere. When he attains to the state of perfection, he will receive these qualities; his heart becomes purified, his spirit enlightened, his soul is sensitized and tender -- all through his great strength. This is the difference between the perfect man and the child. Both have the underlying qualities of simplicity and sincerity -- the child through the power of weakness and the man through the power of strength.

order.why: Read the reported call to a childlike heart.
Connect adult purity with the hope of the Kingdom.
shortened: Their hearts are like pure mirrors. They are in utmost cleanliness. When the hearts of the grown people become as pure then the Kingdom of God will come on earth. Children in their childhood are beloved because of the purity of their hearts.

order.why: Retain the brief reported appreciation of children.
shortened: Truly, the hearts of the children are very pure.

order.why: Read freedom from worldly ambition in childhood.
Keep the reference to Christ’s teaching about children.
Retain the reported delicacy of those hearts.
Join childlike sensitivity with investigation of reality.
Keep the welcome to people with seeing eyes.
Read the invitation to turn the spirit heavenward.
Retain the reported wish for transparency.
Imagine hearts as pages made luminous.
Let the heart become a rose garden.
shortened: I cherish the hope that through the grace of Baha thy face may be illumined with faithfulness and thy heart may, through purity, become the envy of the rose garden.

order.why: Keep the peacock’s plumage as a holiness image.
Read fish and birds through their distinct elements.
Read the extended Iqan account of seeking without bias.
shortened: But, O my brother, when a true seeker determineth to take the step of search in the path leading to the knowledge of the Ancient of Days, he must, before all else, cleanse and purify his heart, which is the seat of the revelation of the inner mysteries of God, from the obscuring dust of all acquired knowledge, and the allusions of the embodiments of satanic fancy. He must purge his breast, which is the sanctuary of the abiding love of the Beloved, of every defilement, and sanctify his soul from all that pertaineth to water and clay, from all shadowy and ephemeral attachments. He must so cleanse his heart that no remnant of either love or hate may linger therein, lest that love blindly incline him to error, or that hate repel him away from the truth.

order.why: Examine both love and hatred as possible barriers to inquiry.
shortened: Furthermore, he must endure every tribulation, embody the utmost purity and sanctity, and renounce the love or hatred of all the peoples of the world, lest his love for one thing hinder him from investigating another, or his hatred for something prevent him from discerning its truth.

order.why: Join purified attention with rational and authoritative arguments.
shortened: O seeker of the True One! If thou wishest divine knowledge and recognition, purify thy heart from all beside God, be wholly attracted to the ideal, beloved One; search for and choose Him and apply thyself to rational and authoritative arguments. For arguments are a guide to the path and by this the heart will be turned unto the Sun of Truth. And when the heart is turned unto the Sun, then the eye will be opened and will recognize the Sun through the Sun itself.

order.why: Read spiritual influence through its effects.
Bring inward preparation to weighing divine questions.
Distinguish reading scripture from understanding it.
shortened: It is easy to read the Holy Scriptures, but it is only with a clean heart and a pure mind that one may understand their true meaning.

order.why: Consider what prior possessions can obscure.
shortened: Among the words of the Most Glorious One - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - are these: "Whoso hath not purified his heart and his breast and his sight and his hearing from that which he possesseth, he shall not be able to understand what hath been revealed in truth in the Tablets of manifest glory."

order.why: Include hearing and sight in preparation for recognition.
shortened: Hasten with pure hearts that ye may attain and discover that which is befitting. Purify yourselves with the water of detachment from covetousness and unseemly deeds, that ye may discover the mystery of the Day of the Self-Subsisting. The Primal Light hath appeared in the Final Day. Through three things shall the Meeting be attained and deliverance made manifest: purity of heart, purity of sight, and purity of hearing from that which hath been heard.

order.why: Ask how names and expectations can become veils.
shortened: Likewise must they purify their hearing and sight to such degree that names will not prevent them from turning towards Him, nor will the veils of beauty and the clouds of majesty hold them back from the Self-Subsisting Lord. In brief, they must sanctify their thoughts from the mention of all else but God, that they may become worthy to turn towards Him and capable of drawing near.

order.why: Enter inquiry with longing and free will.
shortened: O servant! Purify thy heart from all that thou hast heard, then enter with thy heart the holy precincts with longing and free will.

order.why: Connect sanctified perception with recognition and praise.
shortened: Sanctified must be the eye if it is to truly recognize Him, and sanctified must be the tongue if it is to befittingly utter His praise.

order.why: Read hearing and sight as complementary capacities.
shortened: O people! Purify your ears that ye may hear My melodies, then your eyes that ye may behold My beauty. Thus hath God commanded you in all the Tablets and in this Tablet which hath appeared and shone forth from the horizon of the finger of your Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, and God is witness unto this.

order.why: Consider what inward preparation makes discoverable.
Join love with an opening of knowledge.
shortened: Likewise, ask thou of God that the magnet of His love should draw unto thee the knowledge of Him. Once a soul becometh holy in all things, purified, sanctified, the gates of the knowledge of God will open wide before his eyes.

order.why: Read divine love as the teacher of pure hearts.
shortened: If thou remainest firm in the love of God, the wellsprings of divine wisdom will flow from thy heart and tongue, and thou wilt become aware of the meanings of the divine words, for His love hath ever been and shall continue to be the teacher of pure hearts and sanctified souls.

order.why: Consider spiritual perception of unseen realms.
shortened: Know then that the Lord God possesseth invisible realms which the human intellect can never hope to fathom nor the mind of man conceive. When once thou hast cleansed the channel of thy spiritual sense from the pollution of this worldly life, then wilt thou breathe in the sweet scents of holiness that blow from the blissful bowers of that heavenly land.

order.why: Distinguish the universal breeze from receiving its fragrance.
shortened: O ye beloved of Abdu'l-Baha and ye handmaids of the Merciful! It is early morning, and the reviving winds of the Abha Paradise are blowing over all creation, but they can stir only the pure of heart, and only the pure sense can detect their fragrance. Only the perceiving eye beholdeth the rays of the sun; only the listening ear can hear the singing of the Concourse on high.
Today the soft and holy breathings of the Abha Realm are passing over every land, but only the pure in heart draw nigh and derive a benefit therefrom.

order.why: Connect purity, nearness and spiritual discovery.
shortened: The more pure and sanctified the heart of man becomes, the nearer it draws to God, and the light of the Sun of Reality is revealed within it. This light sets hearts aglow with the fire of the love of God, opens in them the doors of knowledge and unseals the divine mysteries so that spiritual discoveries are made possible.

Behold how the sun shines upon all creation, but only surfaces that are pure and polished can reflect its glory and light. The darkened soul has no portion of the revelation of the glorious effulgence of reality; and the soil of self, unable to take advantage of that light, does not produce growth.

order.why: Read effort and self-abnegation alongside understanding.
shortened: He has endowed us with a power to penetrate the realities of things; but we must be self-abnegating, we must have pure spirits, pure intentions, and strive with heart and soul while in the human world to attain everlasting glory.

order.why: Keep purity, joy and truth-seeking together.
Follow the mirror image into knowledge and joy.
shortened: O dear friend! Man can only draw near to the embodied luminosity of heaven and the personified mercifulness of the All-Glorious through nobility of nature, purity of essence, sanctity of soul and conscience, and the power of certitude. Therefore, when a person of pure heart and sanctified mind becomes, mirror-like, free from the rust of attachment to aught else but God, he derives light from the Sun of Reality, becomes a polished surface reflecting divine lights, becomes an unveiler of mysteries, becomes the joy of the righteous, attains to true existence, and is freed from all sorrow.

order.why: Read the reported inward meaning of heaven.
shortened: When the heart is pure and filled with the light of the Spirit, we will know that we are in the true ' Heaven.'

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of finding divine presence within.
Read the heart prepared as a dwelling place.
shortened: The Blessed Perfection has spoken to like effect: "The heart is My room; cleanse it, make it ready, that I may come and dwell in it. Thy spirit is My desire; purify it, that I may visit it."

order.why: Remember the purpose for which hearts are made.
shortened: Say: Deliver your souls, O people, from the bondage of self, and purify them from all attachment to anything besides Me. Remembrance of Me cleanseth all things from defilement, could ye but perceive it.

He hath chosen out of the whole world the hearts of His servants, and made them each a seat for the revelation of His glory. Wherefore, sanctify them from every defilement, that the things for which they were created may be engraven upon them.

order.why: Compare earthly treasure with receptive acceptance.
shortened: The treasures ye have laid up have drawn you far away from your ultimate objective.

Wash from your hearts all earthly defilements, and hasten to enter the Kingdom of your Lord, the Creator of earth and heaven, Who caused the world to tremble and all its peoples to wail, except them that have renounced all things and clung to that which the Hidden Tablet hath ordained.

How many an embodiment of heedlessness who came unto Us with purity of heart have We established upon the seat of Our acceptance; and how many an exponent of wisdom have We in all justice consigned to the fire.

order.why: Explore the heart’s undivided affection.
shortened: Return, then, and cleave wholly unto God, and cleanse thine heart from the world and all its vanities, and suffer not the love of any stranger to enter and dwell therein. Not until thou dost purify thine heart from every trace of such love can the brightness of the light of God shed its radiance upon it, for to none hath God given more than one heart.
And as the human heart, as fashioned by God, is one and undivided, it behoveth thee to take heed that its affections be, also, one and undivided.

order.why: Read the role of innate powers in drawing near.
shortened: He Who is the Dayspring of Truth is, no doubt, fully capable of rescuing from such remoteness wayward souls and of causing them to draw nigh unto His court and attain His Presence. “If God had pleased He had surely made all men one people.” His purpose, however, is to enable the pure in spirit and the detached in heart to ascend, by virtue of their own innate powers, unto the shores of the Most Great Ocean, that thereby they who seek the Beauty of the All-Glorious may be distinguished and separated from the wayward and perverse. Thus hath it been ordained by the all-glorious and resplendent Pen.

order.why: Distinguish spiritual purity from dress.
Locate purification’s essence within the heart.
Read inward freedom alongside outward cleanliness and refinement.
shortened: First in a human being's way of life must be purity, then freshness, cleanliness, and independence of spirit. First must the stream bed be cleansed, then may the sweet river waters be led into it. Chaste eyes enjoy the beatific vision of the Lord and know what this encounter meaneth; a pure sense inhaleth the fragrances that blow from the rose gardens of His grace; a burnished heart will mirror forth the comely face of truth.

order.why: Keep the reported relationship of bodily and inward care.
shortened: Just as the heart - the invisible Shekinah - must be a rosegarden - fragrant, delicate, so also the body must be kept clean and pure - letting the outward appearance be a key to the inward clearness, transparency and purity.

order.why: Read the Bab’s washing counsel within sincere intention.
shortened: Choose ye nothing for yourselves except that ye desire it for God, the Lord of the worlds. Do no deed except that ye act sincerely for God, the Lord of the worlds. Hearken not to any word except that ye hearken through God, for God, the Lord of the worlds. Look not upon anything except that ye look through God, for God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Extend purification across senses, knowledge, actions and pursuits.
Begin the prayer sequence with a renewed conscience.
shortened: Thereupon say:
Create in me a pure heart, O my God, and renew a tranquil conscience within me, O my Hope!

order.why: Ask for a heart like a pearl.
Pray for a spiritual heart and conscience.
shortened: O God! Sanctify me from all else save Thee, purge me from the dross of sins and transgressions and cause me to possess a spiritual heart and conscience.

order.why: Read supplication as the mirror’s polish.
shortened: The heart of man is like a mirror that is covered with dust, and to cleanse it one must continually pray to GOD that it may become clean, and the act of supplication is the polish which erases all worldly desires. The delight of supplicating and entreating before GOD cuts one's heart from the world. When the taste of man is nourished by honey, he never likes to taste any other sweetmeat.

order.why: Follow attentive prayer into daily life.
